blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Recent AI agents can generate playable games, but these games are not necessarily engaging. Mastery is a key source of engagement, yet designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning. We propose PlayCraft, an automated framework that uses a vision-based agent to play games and draws on its detailed play experience to revise them for mastery. Starting from an initial game, PlayCraft alternates between playing and crafting. In the playing stage, a player agent watches the game screen, uses the controls, and pursues the game objective over repeated episodes while retaining memory. After each episode, it reports its progress, outcomes, decisions, and reflections. In the crafting stage, a crafter agent uses these reports to revise the game. It estimates player abilities, predicts performance at different proficiency levels, and compares those predictions with a target learning progression. It diagnoses the game and addresses the gaps by giving players meaningful opportunities to improve through better decisions and execution. We evaluate games in fresh runs with player agents across three intelligence settings, measuring learning gain and learning slope. Compared with the initial games, PlayCraft yields larger learning gains and steeper learning slopes in most games. It also outperforms the baselines on the macro-average of each metric at every intelligence setting.
blocks.zh: 最近的AI代理可以生成可玩游戏,但这些游戏并不一定是参与. Mastery是参与的关键来源,然而它的设计需要广泛的人类游戏和调谐. 我们提议PlayCraft,一个自动化的框架,它使用一个基于视觉的代理游戏,并借鉴其详细的游戏经验来修改它们以供掌握. 从初始游戏开始,PlayCraft在游戏和制作之间替换. 在游戏舞台上,玩家代理观看游戏屏幕,使用控件,在保留内存的同时,在重复的剧集中追求游戏目标. 每集之后,报告其进展、结果、决定和思考。 在制作阶段,一个制作人代理人利用这些报告来修改游戏. 它估计玩家的能力,预测不同熟练级别的表现,并将这些预测与目标学习进度进行比较. 它通过给玩家提供有意义的机会,通过更好的决策和执行来改进,从而判断游戏并解决差距. 我们通过三个智能环境与玩家特工进行新鲜运行评估游戏,衡量学习收益和学习坡度. 与最初的游戏相比,PlayCraft在大多数游戏中产生更大的学习收益和更陡峭的学习坡度. 它的绩效也超过了每个情报环境每个度量的宏观平均基线。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Recent AI agents can generate playable games from human instructions ( Huang et al., 2026 ) , but making these games engaging remains difficult.
A central source of engagement is mastery, which is the process of developing strategies and skills to overcome the challenges of a game ( Koster, 2004 ) .
A game supports mastery when players initially achieve limited success but reach substantially better results as they become more proficient.
This progression motivates repeated play, but designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning.
We therefore study how to automatically generate games that support mastery.
blocks.zh:
近期的AI代理可以从人类指令中生成可玩游戏(Huang等人,2026年),但使得这些游戏的接触仍然很困难.
参与的一个核心来源是掌握,这是制定战略和技能以克服游戏挑战的过程(Koster,2004年)。
游戏支持在玩家一开始取得有限成功,但随着他们的熟练程度提高而取得显著更好的结果时掌握.
这种进步激发了反复播放的动力,但为此而设计需要广泛的人机演奏和调谐.
因此,我们研究如何自动生成支持掌握的游戏.

blocks.en:
Prior work generates games that reward stronger play by using play results from computational players to guide designs ( Togelius and Schmidhuber, 2008 ; Nasir et al., 2026 ) .
However, the strategies these players find through search or game-specific training may differ from those people develop, making their behavior less representative of human play.
Other systems use feedback from repeated playtests to revise generated games ( Huang et al., 2026 ; Wu et al., 2026 ; Chen et al., 2026a ) .
These systems prioritize overall game quality, with limited explicit focus on player learning through practice.
blocks.zh:
前作通过使用计算玩家的游戏结果来引导设计,生成奖励更强游戏的游戏(Togelius and Schmidhuber, 2008;Nasir et al., 2026).
然而,这些玩家通过搜索或游戏特定训练而发现的战略可能与这些人开发的战略不同,使得他们的行为较少代表人类游戏.
其他系统使用反复播放测试的反馈来修改生成的游戏(黄等人,2026年;吴等人,2026年;陈等人,2026a年).
这些系统优先安排游戏的整体质量,对玩家通过练习学习的明显关注有限.

blocks.en:
Recent agents based on foundation models, such as GPT-6 Astra ( OpenAI, 2026a ) , can play 2D and 3D games directly from rendered frames ( Yu, 2026 ; Aggarwal and Welleck, 2026 ) .
They perceive only what the game shows, act through the same controls as human players, and can learn from earlier experience.
They can also report their understanding of the game and the difficulties they encounter.
These capabilities make them suitable simulated players whose experience can shape challenges that reward skillful play.
blocks.zh:
基于基础模型的近期代理商,如GPT-6 Astra(OpenAI,2026a),可以直接从渲染帧(Yu, 2026;Aggarwal and Welleck, 2026)播放2D和3D游戏.
他们只看到游戏显示的东西,通过与人类玩家相同的控制来行动,并且可以学习早期的经验.
他们也可以报告自己对游戏的理解和遭遇的困难.
这些能力使他们成为合适的模拟玩家,他们的经验可以塑造挑战,奖励技能丰富的游戏.

blocks.en:
We propose PlayCraft, an automated framework that starts from an initial playable game and alternates between playing and crafting stages.
In the playing stage, a foundation-model player agent observes rendered frames and interacts with the game through the provided controls.
It plays a series of episodes, gaining experience with the mechanics and challenges it encounters.
The game resets between attempts, while the player agent retains its memory and the lessons it has learned.
After each episode, it writes a report covering its progress, outcomes, decisions, and reflections.
In the crafting stage, a crafter agent uses these reports to diagnose and revise the game to promote engagement through mastery.
It first estimates the baseline abilities that the player agent has before playing the game.
Using these abilities and the observed play, it estimates player performance in the current game at beginner, intermediate, and expert levels.
It then identifies gaps between these estimates and a target progression, defined by performance anchors relative to the expected expert outcome.
Lastly, it addresses these gaps by revising the game to provide meaningful opportunities for better decisions and execution, while preserving the objectives and core identity of the game.
blocks.zh:
我们提议PlayCraft,一种自动框架,从最初的可玩游戏开始,在游戏和制作阶段之间替代。
在游戏舞台上,一个基础模型的玩家代理观察通过所提供的控制使帧和与游戏互动.
它播放了一系列的剧集,获得力学方面的经验和遇到的挑战.
游戏在尝试之间重播,而玩家代理则保留其内存和吸取的教训.
每集之后,它都会写一份报告,阐述其进展、结果、决定和思考。
在制作阶段,一个制作人代理人利用这些报告来诊断和修改游戏,通过掌握促进接触.
它首先估计玩家代理在玩游戏前的基线能力.
利用这些能力和被观察的游戏,它估计了当前游戏中初学者,中级人物和专家级别的玩家表现.
然后确定这些估计数与目标进展之间的差距,根据预期专家成果的业绩基准加以界定。
最后,它通过修订游戏来弥补这些差距,为更好的决策和执行提供有意义的机会,同时保留游戏的目标和核心特征.

blocks.en:
We conduct experiments covering ten 2D and 3D games with varied execution and planning demands.
The games are evaluated at three agent intelligence settings using the visual play protocol from the playing stage.
We use gains in agent performance across episodes as a proxy for mastery, assuming that the learning patterns of the player agent resemble those of human players.
We compute learning gain and learning slope ( Li et al., 2026 ) for the initial games, games produced by PlayCraft, and games revised through code analysis alone or playtesting with policy-based controllers.
Compared with the initial games, PlayCraft increases macro-average learning gain by 2.7, 14.0, and 21.9 percentage points at the Low, Medium, and High intelligence settings, respectively.
Its macro-average learning slope increases by 2.09 and 2.64 at Medium and High, respectively, and is nearly tied at Low.
PlayCraft also achieves higher macro-averages for both metrics than either baseline at every intelligence setting.
blocks.zh:
我们进行实验,涵盖10个2D和3D游戏,需要不同的执行和规划要求.
游戏在三个代理智能设置上使用游戏舞台上的视觉游戏协议进行评估.
我们利用各集的代理性表现收益作为掌握的代名词,假设玩家代理的学习模式与人类玩家相似.
我们计算学习增益和学习斜率(Li et al., 2026),用于初始游戏,PlayCraft制作的游戏,以及仅通过代码分析或通过基于政策的控制器进行播放测试而修改的游戏.
与最初的游戏相比,PlayCraft在低,中,高智能设置中分别增加了2.7,14.0和21.9个百分点的宏平均学习收益.
它的宏观平均学习坡度在中高分上分别增加了2.09和2.64,在低分上几乎捆绑.
PlayCraft还实现了两个度量的宏观平均值高于每个智能环境的基线。

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Mastery and player experience. Game design theory has long tied engagement to learning. Koster (2004) argues that games are fun because players learn their patterns and develop mastery, and self-determination theory links enjoyment and continued play to perceived competence ( Ryan et al., 2006 ) . Linehan et al. (2014) analyze how successful puzzle games pace their challenges as players learn.
Experience-driven procedural content generation ( Yannakakis and Togelius, 2011 ) uses computational models of player experience to guide the search for
game content that elicits a desired experience.
PlayCraft takes mastery as its design goal and uses a surrogate based on gains in player performance across repeated attempts.
blocks.zh:
掌握和玩家经验. 游戏设计理论长期将接触与学习挂钩. Koster(2004年)认为,游戏很有趣,因为玩家学习他们的模式并发展掌握,自决理论将享受和继续游戏与感知的能力联系起来(Ryan等人,2006年). Linehan等人(2014年)分析了玩家学习时拼图游戏的成功步伐.
经验驱动的程序内容生成(Yannakakis and Togelius, 2011) 使用玩家经验的计算模型来指导搜索
游戏内容,可以引发想要的体验.
PlayCraft以精通为设计目标,在反复尝试中根据玩家性能的增益使用代号.

blocks.en:
Automatic game design with computational players. Automatic playtesting uses computational players to simulate distinct play styles ( Holmgrd et al., 2018 ) , estimate difficulty for human players ( Gudmundsson et al., 2018 ) , and predict player churn ( Roohi et al., 2021 ) .
Agent performance can also guide the selection of candidate designs or the tuning of game parameters. Togelius and Schmidhuber (2008) evolve the rules of small grid games and score each game by how well neural controllers learn to play it, treating learnability as a surrogate for fun.
Later work uses self-play to evaluate board-game quality ( Browne and Maire, 2010 ) and exact game-theoretic values for restricted play to assess competitive balance ( Jaffe et al., 2012 ) .
Other systems use the win rate of a stronger agent against a weaker one as a proxy for game depth ( Liu et al., 2017 ; Todd et al., 2024 ) .
Mortar ( Nasir et al., 2026 ) applies this idea to game code, evolving game mechanics through LLM-driven quality-diversity search and rewarding games in which fixed agents (MCTS with different budgets, random, and no-op) rank in their expected order of skill.
Fly, Fail, Fix ( Zook et al., 2025 ) uses a pretrained DQN to play Flappy Bird .
It then uses GPT-4.1 ( OpenAI, 2025 ) to adjust the pipe parameters (gap size, spacing, and speed) based on the resulting play metrics and frame strips to bring the score closer to a target.
Computational players that rely on search or game-specific training may behave differently from humans, require substantial computation to learn unfamiliar games, and offer little insight into their decisions or difficulties.
To better approximate human play, PlayCraft uses a foundation-model agent that infers mechanics from visual cues, draws on prior knowledge to begin playing, and reflects on earlier attempts to improve.
The agent can also explain its decisions and link difficulties to specific situations in the game.
blocks.zh:
与计算玩家进行自动游戏设计. 自动播放测试使用计算玩家模拟不同的游戏风格(Holmgrd等人,2018年),估计人类玩家的难度(Gudmundsson等人,2018年),并预测玩家churn(Roohi等人,2021年).
代理性能还可以指导选择候选设计或调试游戏参数. Togelius和Schmidhuber (2008年)通过神经控制器如何学习游戏来演绎小格格游戏的规则,并给每个游戏打分,将学习可学性作为游戏的代孕.
后期作品使用自玩来评价棋盘-游戏质量(Browne and Maire,2010)以及限定游戏的确切游戏理论值来评价竞争平衡(Jaffe等人,2012年).
其他系统则使用较强代理商对较弱代理商的胜率作为游戏深度的代名词(Liu等人,2017年;Todd等人,2024年).
Mortar (Nasir et al., 2026) 将这一想法应用于游戏代码,通过LLM驱动的质量多样性搜索和奖励游戏来演化游戏力学,其中固定代理(MCTS,预算不同,随机,不op)按预期的技能顺序排列.
Fly, Fault, Fix(Zook等人,2025年)使用预训的DQN来演奏Flappy Bird .
然后它利用GPT-4.1(OpenAI,2025年),根据由此产生的播放度量和帧条来调整管道参数(gap大小,间隔,速度),使得分更接近目标.
依赖搜索或游戏特定训练的计算玩家可能行为与人类不同,需要大量的计算来学习不熟悉的游戏,对其决定或困难也很少提供见解.
为了更近似于人类游戏,PlayCraft使用一个基础模型代理,从视觉提示中推断力学,借鉴先前的知识开始演奏,并反思早先的改进尝试.
代理商还可以解释其决定,并将困难与游戏中的具体情况联系起来.

blocks.en:
LLM-based game generation and revision. LLM agents now generate playable games by decomposing prompts into hierarchical plans, coordinating specialized development and review agents, and reusing skills and knowledge from earlier projects ( Earle et al., 2024 ; Yin et al., 2026 ; Jiang et al., 2026 ; Hu et al., 2026 ) . Benchmarks evaluate the resulting games through multimodal judging and interaction-based tests ( Zhang et al., 2025b ; Luo et al., 2026 ; Chen et al., 2026b ) .
Several recent systems use playtest feedback to refine the games they generate.
Play2Code ( Huang et al., 2026 ) alternates HTML game generation with playtesting by a rubric-blind GUI agent that returns gameplay traces and actionable feedback.
RSIGame ( Wu et al., 2026 ) uses targeted playtests to diagnose issues and verify edits, while a separate monitor compares builds and retains the one it judges best.
Recursive Game Creator ( Chen et al., 2026a ) organizes recursive refinement around Designer, Builder, Player, and Reviewer roles.
Its Player writes reusable policies that act through programmatic interfaces, and its Reviewer uses the resulting trajectories to infer player preferences and recommend changes.
These systems aim to enhance overall game quality.
PlayCraft focuses on mastery, revising games so that players can improve their performance through practice.
blocks.zh:
基于LLM的游戏生成和修订. LLM代理商现在通过将提示分解成分级计划,协调专业开发和审查代理商,以及重新使用早期项目的技能和知识来生成可玩游戏(Earle等人,2024年;Yin等人,2026年;Jiang等人,2026年;Hu等人,2026年). 基准通过多模式判断和基于互动的测试来评价所产生的游戏(Zhang等人,2025b;Luo等人,2026b;Chen等人,2026b)。
最近几个系统利用播放测试反馈来完善它们产生的游戏.
Play2Code (Huang et al., 2026) 副游戏 HTML 生成,由 RUB-BUIND GUI 代理器进行播放测试,返回游戏播放痕迹和可操作反馈.
RSIGame(Wu等人,2026年)使用有针对性的播放测试来诊断问题和核实编辑,而一个单独的显示器则比较建构并保留它判断最好的一个.
递归游戏创造者(Chen et al., 2026a)围绕设计者,构建者,玩家,和评论者角色组织递归改进.
它的玩家写出通过程序界面行事的可重复使用的政策,它的审阅员利用由此产生的轨迹来推断玩家偏好和建议修改.
这些系统旨在提高游戏的整体质量.
PlayCraft专注于掌握,修订游戏,以便玩家通过练习提高自己的性能.

blocks.en:
Visual game-playing agents. Agents can play commercial video games through the same interface as human players, choosing keyboard and mouse actions based on screen observations ( Tan et al., 2024 ; SIMA Team, 2024 ) .
Early benchmarks found that agents often struggled to use those observations to make sustained progress toward game objectives ( Paglieri et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025a ) .
More recent benchmarks demonstrate the visual game-playing capabilities of GPT-6 Astra ( OpenAI, 2026a ) .
On LOLPlay, it completed 9 of 36 League of Legends tasks using screenshots ( Yu, 2026 ) .
In the online track of GameHorizon-Bench, it completed 9 of 20 multi-step tasks in Minecraft ( Wang et al., 2026 ) .
On Gym-Anything-RT, it passed 9% of the minigames in real time and 75% with the games paused between decisions ( Aggarwal and Welleck, 2026 ) .
PlayCraft draws on these advances in visual gameplay by using a foundation-model agent that observes rendered frames and acts through the same controls available to human players.
blocks.zh:
视觉游戏游戏代理商. 代理商可以通过与人类玩家相同的界面进行商业电子游戏,根据屏幕观测选择键盘和鼠标动作(Tan等人,2024年;SIMA Team,2024年).
早期基准发现,代理人往往难以利用这些观测结果在实现游戏目标方面取得持续进展(Paglieri等人,2025年;Zhang等人,2025年a)。
较近期的基准展示了GPT-6 Astra(OpenAI,2026a)的视觉游戏玩法能力.
在LOLPlay上,它使用截图完成了36个传奇联盟任务中的9个(Yu,2026).
在GameHorizon-Bench的在线赛道上,它完成了Minecraft(Wang等人,2026年)20项多步任务中的9项.
在Gym-Anything-RT上,它实时通过了9%的迷你游戏,75%的游戏在决定间暂停(Aggarwal and Welleck, 2026).
PlayCraft在视觉游戏游戏中借鉴了这些进步,使用一个基础模型代理,通过人类玩家可用的相同控制来观察渲染的帧和行为.

blocks.en:
Agent learning from experience. Agents can draw on earlier play when facing a new attempt or task. Reflexion carries lessons from completed trials into later attempts ( Shinn et al., 2023 ) , and Voyager stores acquired skills for reuse in new tasks ( Wang et al., 2023 ) .
Learn2Play Bench measures agent improvement over repeated attempts at text games with unfamiliar rules, using metrics such as the learning gain between early and late episodes ( Li et al., 2026 ) .
PlayCraft uses experience from the player agent to guide game design and assesses support for mastery through performance gains across episodes.
blocks.zh:
特工从经验中学习。 在面对新的尝试或任务时,特工可以借鉴早期的游戏. 反射法将已完成的试验的经验教训带入以后的尝试(Shinn等人,2023年),Voyager商店获得了在新任务中再利用的技能(Wang等人,2023年).
Learn2Play Leading Teachs用早期和晚期的学习收益等衡量标准衡量文字游戏的反复尝试,
PlayCraft利用玩家代理的经验指导游戏设计,并通过各集的性能收益评估对掌握的支持.

blocks.en: 3 Methodology
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en: 3.1 Foundation Models as Players
blocks.zh: 3.1 基金会模式作为玩家

blocks.en:
Recent AI agents based on foundation models such as GPT-6 can play both 2D and 3D games like human players.
Given a brief game instruction, they infer the mechanics from screenshots, interact through the provided controls, observe the outcomes, and improve their performance with continued play.
Three properties make them suitable as automatic players:
blocks.zh:
最近基于GPT-6等基础模型的AI代理可以像人类玩家一样同时玩2D游戏和3D游戏.
鉴于一个简短的游戏指令,他们从截图中推断出力学,通过所提供的控制进行互动,观察结果,并通过继续播放来提高他们的性能.
三个属性使它们适合作为自动玩家:

blocks.en: • They can draw on prior knowledge of game genres, controls, and conventions to begin playing an arbitrary game. • They can play from rendered frames and use the same controls as human players, so their performance can reflect the visual cues and control demands that shape human play. • They can learn across attempts by testing hypotheses about rules and strategies, then carrying the lessons into later episodes. They can also report on their play experience, describing the situations they encounter and sharing their perspective on the game. Together, these capabilities let a foundation-model agent learn through repeated play and provide valuable information for game design.

blocks.en: 3.2 PlayCraft
blocks.zh: 3.2 PlayCraft 游戏

blocks.en: 3.2.1 Overview

PlayCraft is an automated framework that designs games for mastery. It starts from an initial playable game G 0 G_{0} and produces revised games G 1 , … , G K G_{1},\dots,G_{K} .
Each play–craft iteration k = 0 , … , K − 1 k=0,\ldots,K-1 has two stages.
In the playing stage, the player agent receives a brief game instruction and pursues the game objective over repeated episodes of G k G_{k} .
It retains its memory across episodes and writes a report after each one. The reports form the play record passed to the crafting stage.
In the crafting stage, the crafter agent uses the play records to diagnose the game.
It estimates baseline player abilities and compares expected performance at different proficiency levels with predefined anchors.
It then proposes and implements changes that address the gaps and give players room to improve through better decisions and execution, producing G k + 1 G_{k+1} for the next iteration.
Figure 1 illustrates the PlayCraft loop.

blocks.en: 3.2.2 Playing Stage
blocks.zh: 3.2.2 播放阶段

blocks.en:
Setup. The player agent begins with a fresh context containing a brief game instruction that states the objective, basic rules, and available controls.
The player agent observes only rendered frames and cannot inspect the game code or access the Internet.
It generates every control action through model inference rather than writing a program to control the game.
blocks.zh:
设置. 玩家代理开始使用新上下文,包含一个简短的游戏指令,说明目标,基本规则,以及可用的控制.
玩家代理只观察渲染帧,不能检查游戏代码或访问互联网.
它通过模型推论生成每个控制动作,而不是写一个程序来控制游戏.

blocks.en:
Interaction. A run consists of E E episodes. Each episode ends when the game reaches a defined endpoint or the active play budget T T is exhausted.
Game frames are captured at intervals of O O , and the player agent makes a decision at intervals of W W .
At each decision, it receives the frames captured during the preceding decision interval and returns an action plan for the next interval of play.
The plan is a sequence of A A control actions, each lasting for a duration W / A W/A . A control action is a combination of keys, mouse buttons, and mouse movements.
While the plan executes, the game advances and renders frames, which are included in the next decision request so that the player observes the consequences of its previous plan.
Game timers and animations pause while the model generates the next action plan, so decision latency does not consume play time.
With each plan, the player also reports the visible result, such as the current score, and provides brief notes on its observations and choices.
blocks.zh:
互动. 跑步由E E集组成. 每集在游戏达到定义的终点或活跃的游戏预算TT耗尽时结束.

在每个决定中,它都会收到在前一个决定间隔期间捕获的帧,并返回下一个游戏间隔的行动计划.
计划是A控制动作的序列,每次持续时间为W / A W/A. 一个控制动作是将密钥,鼠标按钮,鼠标移动组合起来.

玩家还用每个计划报告可见的结果,如当前得分,并简要说明其观察和选择.

blocks.en:
Learning across episodes. The player agent maintains a single conversation throughout a run.
The game resets between episodes, but the player retains its memory.
After each episode, the player reviews its play and writes a report covering (1) the starting conditions; (2) its progress, including milestones and failures; (3) the final result; (4) its key decisions and the alternatives it considered; (5) its perception of the game, including its understanding of the mechanics, points of confusion, perceived difficulty, and discrepancies between expected and observed outcomes; and (6) the lessons it learned.
The player then updates a consolidated set of natural-language lessons, retaining supported lessons, merging overlapping ones, and revising or removing contradicted ones.
It begins the next episode with its memory of earlier attempts and the updated lessons.
The reports of all episodes form the play record of the run, which is passed to the crafting stage.
blocks.zh:

玩家随后更新了一套合并的自然语言课,保留了支持的课,合并了重叠课,并修改或删除了矛盾课.
它以对以前尝试的记忆和最新的教训开始下集.
所有剧集的报告都形成了跑步的剧情记录,该记录被传递到制作阶段.

blocks.en: 3.2.3 Crafting Stage
blocks.zh: 3.2.3 工艺阶段

blocks.en:
Design targets. The crafter agent revises the game toward two targets.
The first is to ensure that players at each proficiency level can meet the corresponding predefined performance target.
The most skilled players should be able to complete the objective within the active play budget T T . In games without an objective, they should be able to experience the core loop and major challenges within that budget. Their expected result defines the 100% reference.
Beginners and intermediate players should achieve r 0 % r_{0}\% and r 1 % r_{1}\% of the expert reference, respectively, with r 0 < r 1 r_{0}<r_{1} .
These results must come from strategies that would remain advantageous without the time limit.
The second is to give players meaningful opportunities to improve through better decisions and execution.
The game should make the benefits, costs, and risks of different choices clear and allow expected performance to continue rising as players gain skill.
blocks.zh:
设计目标. 工匠代理修改游戏面向两个目标.
第一是确保每个熟练级别的玩家都能达到相应的预设的性能目标.
最熟练的球员应该能够在活跃的游戏预算TT范围内完成目标. 在没有目标的游戏中,他们应当能够体验该预算的核心循环和重大挑战。 他们的预期结果界定了100%的参考。
初学者和中间玩家应分别实现专家参考文献的 r% r% r% 0 和 r% 1% r% 1 ,其中 r < r 1 r% 0 r% 1 } 。
这些结果必须来自没有时间限制仍然有利的战略。
第二是给参与者提供有意义的机会,通过更好的决策和执行来改进。
游戏应明确不同选择的好处、成本和风险,并使预期表现随着玩家技能的提高而继续增加。

blocks.en:
Active play budget. We assume that players have a finite active play budget T T , which can be set arbitrarily large.
Introducing T T provides a reference range for player performance, allowing the crafter agent to identify and address gaps between estimated performance and the anchors.
Changing T T can affect the progression of the resulting game because the crafter uses play observed within that budget as evidence for its design.
blocks.zh:
积极发挥预算. 我们假设玩家有一个有限的活跃游戏预算TT,可以任意设定大额.
引入T T为玩家的性能提供了一个参考范围,使制作者代理能够识别并解决估计性能与锚之间的空隙.
改变TT会影响由此而来游戏的发展,因为制作者使用该预算范围内观察到的游戏作为设计的证据.

blocks.en:
Diagnosis. The crafter agent reads the game instruction, the play records of all available runs, and the archived history of earlier iterations.
Because E E episodes may not suffice for the player agent to reach expert-level performance, the crafter agent cannot determine the 100% reference directly from the records.
It therefore first estimates the baseline abilities that the player agent has before playing the game, including screen perception, control execution, and strategy discovery.
A player without prior experience of a game is not necessarily unskilled.
From these abilities and the observed play, it estimates the expected results of beginner, intermediate, and expert players in the current game and compares them with the anchors.
Where the estimates deviate from the anchors, it diagnoses the causes, considering entry difficulty; demands on understanding, perception, and execution; opportunities for strategic choice; reward structure; challenge progression; and performance ceiling.
If an earlier proposal exists, it also checks which expectations in that proposal the new records support, contradict, or leave untested.
It then chooses between building on the earlier direction and exploring a new one.
blocks.zh:
诊断. 制作人代理阅读了游戏指令,所有可用运行的游戏记录,以及早期迭代的存档历史.
由于E E 事件可能不足以让玩家代理达到专家级的性能,因此制作者代理无法直接从记录中确定100%的参考.
因此,它首先估计玩家代理在玩游戏前的基线能力,包括屏幕感知,控制执行,以及策略发现.
玩家没有之前的游戏经验并不一定是非熟练的.
从这些能力和被观察的游戏中,它估计了当前游戏中初学者,中级人物和专家玩家的预期结果,并将其与主播进行比较.
如果估计数偏离主线,则考虑到进入困难、对理解、感知和执行的要求、战略选择机会、奖励结构、挑战进展和业绩上限,分析原因。
如果有早先的提议,它也会检查新记录中哪些期望支持、相互矛盾或不经过检验。
然后它选择在更早的方向上发展,探索新的方向.

blocks.en:
Proposal. The crafter agent then writes a focused design proposal.
It prioritizes distinctive changes or additions that enable new strategies and meaningful choices while preserving the defining interactions of the game.
It keeps the design coherent and simple, weighing the learning benefit of each rule against the complexity it adds.
It builds challenges on the baseline abilities of the player rather than assuming that unfamiliar mechanics alone will limit beginner performance.
The revised game must remain visually clear, conveying objects, actions, and consequences through presentation and behavior rather than added indicators.
The proposal describes each change and the findings that motivate it.
It also states the expected experience and results for beginner, intermediate, and expert players, along with the basis and uncertainty of those estimates.
blocks.zh:
提议。 工匠代理人随后写出重点设计方案.
它优先考虑独特的变化或添加,从而能够制定新的战略和有意义的选择,同时保持游戏的决定性互动.
它保持设计的一致性和简洁性,权衡每个规则的学习效益与它增加的复杂性.
它根据玩家的基线能力构建挑战,而不是假设不熟悉的力学本身会限制初学者的性能.
修改后的游戏必须保持视觉清晰,通过展示和行为来传达对象,行动和后果,而不是增加指标.
提案描述了每项改变以及促使改变的结论。
报告还说明了初学者、中级参与者和专家参与者的预期经验和结果,以及这些估计的基础和不确定性。

blocks.en:
Implementation. In a separate session, the crafter agent implements the proposal.
For each proposed change, the crafter identifies the intended player-facing outcome and specifies observable acceptance checks.
It then modifies the game code, implementing foundational changes before those that depend on them.
It verifies the result by running builds and automated checks, exercising the affected gameplay, and inspecting the affected visuals in the actual renderer.
It then corrects any discrepancies.
It records deviations from the proposal with their reasons and updates the game instruction to state only the objective, basic rules, and available controls, leaving the rest for players to discover.
blocks.zh:
执行。 在另外一届会议上,制作人代理人执行提案。
对于每一项拟议的更改,制作者都确定预期的玩家阵容,并具体说明可观察到的接受检查。
然后它修改了游戏代码,在依赖它们的人之前执行基础修改.
它通过运行建构和自动检查,行使受影响的游戏玩法,以及检查实际渲染器中受影响的视觉,来验证结果.
然后纠正任何不一致之处。
它记录了与提案的偏差及其原因,并更新了游戏指令,只说明目标,基本规则,以及可用的控制,剩下的则留给玩家发现.

For each game, we provide the player with brief instructions covering the objective, basic rules, and controls.

blocks.en: 4.1.2 Comparison methods
blocks.zh: 4.1.2 比较方法

blocks.en:
We compare PlayCraft with two methods that use different evidence for game revision: • Code uses code analysis by a coding agent (Codex), without evidence from a player agent. • Policy generates 10 policy-based controllers that act on the internal game state to collect playtesting evidence.
The controllers do not retain experience across attempts.
This method adapts the generated-policy approach of Recursive Game Creator ( Chen et al., 2026a ) . Both methods use the same design targets, proposal and implementation procedure, and model settings as PlayCraft, with diagnosis and design guided by the evidence available to each method.
Both methods start from the same initial games as PlayCraft and perform 3 revision iterations.

blocks.en: 4.1.3 Evaluation protocol
blocks.zh: 4.1.3 评价协议

blocks.en:
We evaluate the initial games and the final games produced by Code, Policy, and PlayCraft in fresh, independent runs using the visual playing setup described above.
We control player intelligence through 3 combinations of model and reasoning effort, as shown in Table 1 .
The labels Low, Medium, and High identify these experimental settings.
Action planning and episode review use the same model within each setting.
Each initial or final game is evaluated in 3 independent runs of 10 episodes at each intelligence setting, yielding 9 runs in total.
blocks.zh:

标签中低、中、高标识这些实验设置。
行动规划和剧集审查在每个场合使用相同的模式.
每个初始或最终的游戏在每集智能设定中以3集10集的独立运行来评价,总共产生9集.

blocks.zh: 表1:用于评价的玩家智能设置. 集评包括经验报告和教训更新.

blocks.en:
We measure performance by the final game score, except in Desert Racing .
In Desert Racing , the objective prioritizes completed laps, then checkpoint progress, with shorter completion time breaking ties.
We summarize this outcome as the number of checkpoints cleared divided by elapsed active race time, rewarding greater progress and faster completion.
We use the observed outcome of each episode directly.
blocks.zh:
我们用最后的比赛成绩来衡量表现, 除了沙漠赛车。
在沙漠赛跑中,目标优先完成几圈,然后是检查站的进展,缩短完成时间,断开联系。
我们总结了这一结果,因为清除的检查站数目除以经过了积极的赛车时间,这有利于取得更大的进展和更快的完成。
我们直接使用每集的观测结果.

blocks.en: 4.2 Evaluation metrics
blocks.zh: 4.2 评价尺度

blocks.en:
We assess support for mastery through performance improvement across repeated episodes of a fixed game.
We report learning gain to measure overall improvement, and learning slope to summarize the direction and rate of performance change across all episodes.
blocks.zh:
我们通过在固定游戏的反复播放中改进表现来评估对掌握的支持。
我们报告学习收益以衡量总体改善,学习斜度以总结所有各阶段的业绩变化方向和速度。

blocks.en:
Revision can change the attainable performance range, so we normalize performance separately for each game and method, including the initial games.
We divide each episode outcome by the maximum value among the 90 outcomes for that game and method, pooling 3 intelligence settings, 3 runs per setting, and 10 episodes per run.
blocks.zh:
修订可以改变可实现的性能范围,因此我们将每个游戏和方法,包括初始游戏,分别实现性能正常化.
我们把每一集的结果 以最大值来划分 在游戏与方法的90个结果之间, 集合3个智能设置, 3个运行每个设定, 10个运行。

blocks.en:
We compute both measures for each run, then average their values across the 3 runs within each intelligence setting.
For learning slope, fitting each run and averaging the slopes gives the same result as fitting the mean performance at each episode, since all runs have the same episode indices and fitting weights.
For each intelligence setting, we compute the macro-average of the 10 per-game means.
Both measures use normalized performance, so the macro-average summarizes learning across games with different performance scales while giving each game equal weight.
blocks.zh:
我们计算每场比赛的两种度量, 然后平均在3次比赛的数值 在每个情报范围内进行。
就学习坡度而言,每跑和平均坡度的结果与每集的平均表现相同,因为所有跑步都有相同的插曲指数和适当的权重。
对于每个智能环境,我们计算每局10的宏观平均值。
这两种度量法都采用常态化的性能,因此宏观平均值总结了不同性能尺度的游戏间的学习,同时给予每款游戏同等的权重.

blocks.en: 4.3 Results
blocks.zh: 4.3 结果

blocks.en:
According to Table 2 , PlayCraft has the largest macro-average learning gain under all 3 intelligence settings.
Under the Low setting, PlayCraft reaches a macro-average learning gain of 13.7 percentage points.
It outperforms the initial games by +2.7, with higher gains in 8 of 10 games.
It also outperforms Code by +6.3 (higher gains in 6 of 10 games) and Policy by +1.4 (higher gains in 6 of 10 games).
Under the Medium setting, PlayCraft reaches a macro-average learning gain of 31.5 percentage points.
It outperforms the initial games by +14.0, with higher gains in 9 of 10 games.
It also outperforms Code by +8.0 (higher gains in 6 of 10 games) and Policy by +15.3 (higher gains in 8 of 10 games).
Under the High setting, PlayCraft reaches a macro-average learning gain of 34.3 percentage points.
It outperforms the initial games by +21.9, with higher gains in 8 of 10 games.
It also outperforms Code by +18.2 (higher gains in 7 of 10 games) and Policy by +11.9 (higher gains in 7 of 10 games).
blocks.zh:
根据表2,PlayCraft在所有3智能设置下拥有最大的宏观平均学习收益.
在Low设置下,PlayCraft达到了13.7个百分点的宏观平均学习收益.
它以+2.7的成绩超过了最初的游戏,在10场比赛中的8场获得更高的收益.
它还以+6.3(10场游戏中的6场获得更高的收益)和+1.4(10场游戏中的6场获得更高的收益)超越了代码.
在中度设置下,PlayCraft的宏观平均学习收益达到31.5个百分点.
它以+14.0超越了最初的游戏,在10场比赛中的9场获得更高的收益.
它还以+8.0(10场游戏中的6场获得更高的收益)和+15.3(10场游戏中的8场获得更高的收益)超越了代码.
在High设置下,PlayCraft达到34.3个百分点的宏观平均学习收益.
它以+21.9的成绩超过了最初的游戏,在10场比赛中的8场获得更高的收益.
它还以+18.2(10场游戏中的7场获得更高的收益)和+11.9(10场游戏中的7场获得更高的收益)超越了代码.

blocks.en:
According to Table 3 , PlayCraft has the largest macro-average learning slope under the Medium and High settings.
Under the Low setting, PlayCraft reaches a macro-average learning slope of 1.95.
It is nearly tied with the initial games (trailing by about 0.0033), and it achieves steeper slopes in 7 of 10 games.
It outperforms Code by +0.80 (steeper slopes in 6 of 10 games) and Policy by +0.13 (steeper slopes in 6 of 10 games).
Under the Medium setting, PlayCraft reaches a macro-average learning slope of 4.61.
It outperforms the initial games by +2.09, with steeper slopes in 9 of 10 games.
It also outperforms Code by +1.13 (steeper slopes in 7 of 10 games) and Policy by +1.99 (steeper slopes in 8 of 10 games).
Under the High setting, PlayCraft reaches a macro-average learning slope of 4.74.
It outperforms the initial games by +2.64, with steeper slopes in 7 of 10 games.
It also outperforms Code by +2.41 (steeper slopes in 7 of 10 games) and Policy by +1.54 (steeper slopes in 7 of 10 games).
blocks.zh:
根据表3,PlayCraft在中高环境下拥有最大的宏观平均学习坡度.
在Low设置下,PlayCraft达到了1.95的宏观平均学习坡度.
它几乎与最初的游戏捆绑在一起(追逐约0.0033),并在10场比赛的7场中实现了更陡峭的坡度.
它以+0.80(更深的坡度在10场比赛中的6场)和+0.13(更深的坡度在10场比赛中的6场)超过了代码.
在中度设置下,PlayCraft达到4.61的宏观平均学习坡度.
它以+2.09的成绩超过了最初的游戏,在10场比赛的9场中坡度更高.
它还以+1.13(在10场比赛中7场更深的坡度)和+1.99(在10场比赛中8场更深的坡度)超越了政策.
在High设置下,PlayCraft达到了4.74的宏观平均学习坡度.
它以+2.64的成绩超过了最初的游戏,在10场比赛的7场中坡度更高.
它也以+2.41(在10场比赛中7场更深的坡度)和+1.54(在10场比赛中7场更深的坡度)超越了代码.

blocks.en:
These results reflect differences in the evidence used to guide game revision.
Code relies on code analysis without evidence from a player agent.
Policy uses controllers that access internal game state and do not retain experience across attempts.
PlayCraft uses an agent that pursues game objectives through the same interface as human players and learns across episodes by retaining memory and lessons.
The agent reports the strategies it discovers, the difficulties it encounters, and how its performance changes with practice.
This evidence helps the crafter account for existing player abilities and design challenges that reward further learning.
blocks.zh:
这些结果反映了用于指导游戏修改的证据的不同.
代码依赖于代码分析,没有玩家代理的证据.
政策使用控制器,可以访问内部游戏状态,不会在尝试中保留经验.
PlayCraft使用一个代理,通过与人类玩家相同的界面追求游戏目标,并通过保留内存和教训来跨集学习.
代理人报告其发现的战略、遇到的困难以及其业绩如何随着实践而变化。
这些证据帮助制作者说明现有的玩家能力,设计挑战,奖励进一步学习.

blocks.en:
The results also show that learning gain and learning slope generally increase as player intelligence rises.
Players with higher intelligence may discover better strategies and execute them more effectively.
From Low to High, PlayCraft shows the largest increases in both measures.
Its learning gain rises by 20.5 percentage points, compared with 8.7 for Code, 10.0 for Policy, and 1.4 for the initial games.
Its learning slope rises by 2.78, compared with 1.17 for Code, 1.38 for Policy, and 0.14 for the initial games.
The larger increases for PlayCraft suggest that it creates more opportunities for players to improve through stronger play.
blocks.zh:
研究结果还表明,随着玩家智能的提升,学习增益和学习坡度普遍增加.
拥有较高智力的玩家可能会发现更好的策略并更有效地执行.
从低到高,PlayCraft显示两种度量中增幅最大.
其学习增益上升了20.5个百分点,而代码为8.7,政策为10.0,初始游戏为1.4.
其学习坡度上升了2.78,与之相比,代码为1.17,政策为1.38,初始游戏为0.14.
PlayCraft的更大增加表明,它为玩家通过更强的玩法改进创造了更多的机会.

blocks.en:
However, PlayCraft shows smaller increases from Medium to High than from Low to Medium.
For learning gain, the increase is 2.8 percentage points from Medium to High and 17.8 percentage points from Low to Medium.
For learning slope, the corresponding increases are 0.13 and 2.66.
One possible explanation is that PlayCraft uses the Medium player configuration to collect the play records that guide its revisions.
Players in the High setting can handle the resulting challenges more easily.
Over the first 3 episodes, they achieve a mean normalized performance of 47.3%, compared with 38.2% for players in the Medium setting. This higher starting performance may leave less room for improvement in later episodes.
blocks.zh:
然而,PlayCraft显示从中到高的增长比从低到中的增长要小.
就学习收益而言,从中到高的增长为2.8个百分点,从低到中的增长为17.8个百分点。
对于学习坡度,相应的增加值为0.13和2.66.
一个可能的解释是,PlayCraft使用中度播放器配置来收集指导其修改的播放记录.
玩家在High设置中可以更容易地处理由此产生的挑战.
在前三集中,他们实现了47.3%的均匀正常表现,而中场环境下的玩家则为38.2%. 这种较高的起步性能可能为以后各集留下较少的改进余地.

blocks.en:
Figure 3 tracks learning gain and learning slope from each initial game through 3 successive PlayCraft revisions.
Both measures generally increase across revisions, with fluctuations that may reflect variability in gameplay, diagnosis, design, or implementation.
After the final revision, both measures exceed their initial values in 9 of the 10 games.
Both measures drop most sharply in Robotic Arm after the first revision and partially recover after the second.
The first revision introduced wrist sway under load and varied the starting positions of the cans, which may have made transfers harder to execute consistently. Section 4.4 discusses these changes to Robotic Arm in more detail.
blocks.zh:
图3通过连续3次PlayCraft修订来跟踪每个初始游戏的学习增益和学习坡度.
这两项措施在修订过程中普遍增加,波动可能反映游戏、诊断、设计或执行方面的差异。
最终修订后,两项措施在10场比赛的9场中都超过了其初始值.
两项措施在第一次修订后机器人臂最大幅度下降,第二次修订后部分恢复.
第一次修订引入了手腕在负载下摇摆,并改变了罐头的起始位置,这可能使转移更难一致执行. 第4.4节更详细地讨论了机器人臂的这些变化。

Iteration 0 is the initial game. For each game and iteration, performance is normalized by the largest observed outcome. Each point averages three Medium runs.

blocks.en: 4.4 Qualitative analysis
blocks.zh: 4.4 定性分析

blocks.en:
We select 4 games with different demands on planning and execution to understand how each method responds to the skills players must develop.
The cases span rebound control in Breakout , ballistic aiming and target approach in Archery Hunting , object manipulation in Robotic Arm , and route planning and flight under a battery budget in Drone Delivery .
We use the play and revision records to explain how the evidence available to each method shaped its design choices.
blocks.zh:
我们选择了4个对计划和执行有不同要求的游戏,以了解每种方法如何响应技能玩家必须开发的技能.
这些案例跨越了突袭的反弹控制,Archery Hunting的弹道瞄准和瞄准,机器人臂的物体操纵,以及无人机交付的电池预算下的路线规划和飞行。
我们用剧本和审校记录来解释每种方法可用的证据如何塑造其设计选择.

blocks.en:
The initial game requires players to move the paddle to bounce the ball toward the bricks. A brick breaks after a single hit.
The PlayCraft player agent already aimed rebounds deliberately, but clearing isolated bricks required precise follow-up shots.
In the first round, PlayCraft introduced armor that retains damage from underside hits, so one shot can prepare a brick for a later shot.
In subsequent reports, the player described shots that struck a different column than intended and sequences of hits that cleared few bricks.
In the second round, PlayCraft slowed paddle movement for short taps and increased the number of underside hits needed to break a brick to three.
A hit on the side or top could now also clear a contiguous run of damaged neighbors in the same row.
In the third round, PlayCraft made the rebound angle less sensitive to small changes in where the ball strikes near the paddle center.
The ball could now pass through a brick on the third underside hit.
The player can prepare either a direct path through the wall or a sweep along it.
blocks.zh:
最初的比赛要求玩家将划桨移动,使球向砖头反射. 一次命中后一砖断.
PlayCraft玩家代理已经有意瞄准反弹,但清除孤立的砖块需要精确的后续镜头.
在第一轮中,PlayCraft引入了保留了底部命中损伤的装甲,因此一枪就能为后期命中准备砖.
在随后的报告中,玩家描述了击中了与原意不同的栏目的镜头以及清除了几块砖块的命中序列.
在第二轮中,PlayCraft将短水龙头的划桨移动速度减慢,并将击破砖块所需的底部命中次数增加到3次.
击中侧面或顶部,现在也可以清除同一排被破坏的邻居的毗连跑道.
在第三轮中,PlayCraft使得反弹角对球在桨中心附近击落的小变化不太敏感.
球现在可以在第三次底部命中时通过砖块.
玩家可以通过墙壁准备直接路径或沿墙扫荡.

blocks.en:
Code analyzed the collision rules and revised the paddle mechanics so that stopping the paddle before a catch widens its cutting area.
A catch within that area can send the ball through bricks at the base of the wall and into a central passage.
Policy used controller trajectories to identify useful paths into the wall from above and lengthy return trips.
In that revision, breaking a brick from above weakens the remaining bricks in the column below.
The ball continues along its path whenever it destroys a brick.
blocks.zh:
守则分析了碰撞规则,并修改了划桨力学,以便在捕获物扩大其切割面积之前停止划桨。
该地区范围内的捕捉物可以通过墙底的砖块将球送入中央通道.
政策使用控制器的轨迹来识别从上面进入墙壁的有用路径和漫长的回程.
在该修订版中,从上面打碎一块砖块会削弱下面一栏中剩余的砖块.
当球摧毁了一块砖块时,球就沿着它的道路继续前进.

blocks.en:
In Code, players learned to stop the paddle before catches to widen the cutting area, producing substantial progress early.
Later practice focused on steering and positioning for returning balls, but missed catches sometimes prevented these refinements from producing higher scores.
In Policy, players learned to reach exposed tops and sides and exploit weakened columns, but prediction errors after collisions continued to cause missed catches.
At Medium and High, PlayCraft players progressed from safe, near-vertical returns that opened columns to directing shots through those openings for larger clears.
At Low, improvement mainly came from earlier interceptions and controlled column clearing.
Better interception and controlled clearing at Low, together with more effective use of prepared openings at Medium and High, may explain why PlayCraft led on learning gain and slope at all three settings.
blocks.zh:
在"守则"中,玩家学会了在捕捉之前先停止划桨以拓宽剪切区,提前产生实质性进展.
后来的实践侧重于回球的引导和定位,但错过的渔获量有时使这些改进无法产生更高的分数.
在"政策"中,玩家学会了到达暴露的顶部和侧面,并利用被削弱的柱子,但碰撞后的预测错误继续造成渔获错失.
在中高分,PlayCraft的玩家从安全、近垂直的回归中前进,这些回归打开了柱子,通过这些开口来引导拍摄,以获得更大的清晰度。
在Low,改进主要来自早先的拦截和控制列清除.
在Low进行更好的拦截和控制性清理,同时更有效地利用中高处准备的开口,可能解释为什么PlayCraft在所有三个场合都领导学习增益和坡度。

blocks.en:
The initial game requires players to approach targets, choose firing positions, and adjust their aim and draw to account for gravity and wind.
The PlayCraft player agent completed the hunt by closing in on targets and shooting at full draw.
In the first round, PlayCraft added cover and made targets retreat in response to noise from movement, bow releases, and ordinary hits.
A quiet hit on a gold weak spot could leave nearby targets undisturbed.
In the second round, PlayCraft let the player flush targets from one refuge toward the other and extended their exposure during crossings to four seconds.
The player returned to full-draw shots after a quiet shot missed and a prolonged pursuit stalled.
The crafter found that pursuit could still work because targets crossed exposed ground between refuges and ignored new disturbances while retreating.
In the third round, PlayCraft moved the approaches to the escape openings under cover.
When a retreating target reaches a fork, it chooses an escape route based on the latest disturbance it detected.
A quiet hit on a gold weak spot can leave the next target on course. Before a target reaches its fork, a deliberate disturbance can steer it toward an opening where the player can intercept it.
Feedback on ordinary hits now shows where the arrow lands relative to the gold weak spot.
blocks.zh:
最初的游戏要求玩家接近目标,选择射击位置,并调整瞄准和引力以考虑重力和风力.
PlayCraft玩家代理通过关闭目标并全速射击完成狩猎.
在第一轮中,PlayCraft增加了封面,并针对来自运动的噪音,弓释放,以及普通命中,使目标撤退.
静静地击中一个金色的弱点,会使附近的目标不受干扰.
在第二轮中,PlayCraft让玩家将目标从一个避难所冲向另一个避难所,并在穿越时将其曝光时间延长至4秒.
玩家在一次静静的镜头失手,一次长时间的追击停滞后,恢复了全画幅镜头.
工匠发现,由于目标穿越了避难所之间的露天地面,在撤退时忽略了新的骚乱,追捕仍然可以奏效.
在第三轮中,PlayCraft在封面下移动了逃生开关的通道.
当一个撤退的目标到达叉时,它根据它探测到的最新扰动选择一条逃跑路线.
静静地击中一个金牌弱点,可以让下一个目标在航线上. 在目标到达叉子之前,故意的扰动可以引导它走向一个开口,玩家可以拦截它.
对普通命中量的反馈现在显示箭头相对于金色弱点落在什么地方.

blocks.en:
Code used ballistic probes to find that, at close range, full-draw shots could hit even alerted targets without leading them.
It added fallen trunks so players have a reason to arc a lower-draw shot over cover or move to the side for a direct shot.
Policy controllers often moved between firing positions or withheld shots while looking for a clear firing window.
The revision added shared firing areas from which the player can target several marks.
Stone screens limit which targets hear an impact, giving the player more control over which targets retreat.
blocks.zh:
密码使用弹道探测器发现,在近距离上,全长镜头甚至可以击中警戒目标而不引导它们.
它添加了掉落的后备箱,因此玩家有原因对弧进行下拉射过覆盖或移动到侧面直接射击.
政策控制器经常在射击阵地之间移动,或者在寻找清晰的射击窗口时扣下射击.
修订增加了共享射击区域,玩家可以从这些区域瞄准几个标记.
石屏限制哪些目标听到撞击,使玩家对哪些目标退缩有更多的控制.

blocks.en:
In Code, players completed the hunt from the first episode, mostly by moving around cover and using strong draws, then refined their aim for weak-spot hits.
In Policy, players often used quiet draws and waited or repositioned for clearer target faces, reducing speculative shots and conserving arrows.
Both baselines often reached completion early, so later practice mainly improved shot precision and efficiency.
In PlayCraft, brief shooting opportunities and targets retreating behind cover led to missed shots and prolonged searches, often leaving early hunts incomplete.
Players learned to abandon unproductive pursuits, prepare shots for clearer openings, and use directional hit feedback to refine weak-spot aim.
Progress toward completing the hunt, together with improved shot precision, may explain why PlayCraft led on learning gain and slope at all three settings.
blocks.zh:
在"代码"中,玩家从第一集开始完成猎杀,大多是通过绕过封面移动并使用强力的图纸,然后精炼出他们的目标来达到弱点命中.
在"政策"中,玩家经常使用静静的绘图,等待或重新定位以获得更清晰的目标面孔,减少投机镜头和保存箭头.
这两个基线往往提前完成,因此后来的做法主要是提高射程精确度和效率。
在PlayCraft中,短暂的射击机会和隐蔽后退的目标导致射门失守和长时间的搜索,往往留下早期的狩猎不完整.
玩家学会放弃非生产性的追求,为更清晰的开场准备镜头,并使用定向命中反馈来完善弱点目标.
完成狩猎的进展,以及镜头精度的提高,可以解释为什么PlayCraft在所有三个场合都带动学习增益和斜度.

blocks.en:
The initial game requires players to align the gripper, carry each can to the receiver, and release it so it settles on the surface.
The PlayCraft player agent could already transfer cans quickly by using separate landing areas.
In the first round, PlayCraft added wrist sway under load and varied the starting positions of the cans.
In the second round, PlayCraft introduced a rotating receiver.
Delivered cans move with the deck and remain physical obstacles.
As a result, the timing and position of one delivery can affect clearance on the next.
In the third round, PlayCraft revised contact with the receiver after the player reported difficulty withdrawing the gripper and judging whether the deck supported the can.
The deck rotates more slowly when the player rests a held can gently on it.
The player can brace the deck until it stops or release the can while the deck is still moving.
blocks.zh:
最初的游戏要求玩家将抓手对齐,将每个罐头携带到接收器上,然后放出,以便表面安顿下来.
PlayCraft玩家代理可以通过使用单独的登陆区来快速转移罐头.
在第一轮中,PlayCraft在负载下增加了手腕摇摆,并改变了罐头的起始位置.
在第二轮中,PlayCraft引入了旋转接收器.
交付的罐头随甲板移动,并保持物理障碍.
因此,一次交货的时间和位置可能影响下一次交货的清除。
在第三轮,PlayCraft在玩家报告难以撤回抓手并判断甲板是否支持罐头后修改了与接收器的接触.
甲板在玩家躺下时旋转较慢,可以轻轻地放在甲板上.
玩家可以在甲板移动时将甲板架起,直至甲板停止或释放罐头.

blocks.en:
Code used clearance analysis and timed probes to preserve two ways of reaching a stationary receiver.
The player can carry a can through a low opening or over the rail.
The rail, the different can heights, and the ability to tilt the wrist make grip and posture important when clearing obstacles.
Policy controllers struggled to pick up cans, so the final revision moved the obstructing bridges behind the gripping pads, leaving the approach to the claw open.
The revision also lets the player guide a can into place while the stationary receiver supports its weight.
blocks.zh:
密码使用清空分析和定时探测器,以保持两种方式到达固定接收器。
玩家可以通过低开口或过轨携带罐头.
铁轨,不同的高架,手腕的倾斜能力,在清除障碍物时,使握力和姿态变得重要.
政策控制器为捡起罐子而挣扎,因此最终的修订将阻塞的桥梁移到抓住的垫子后面,使接近爪子的路口松开.
修改后还让玩家在固定接收器支持其重量时引导一个罐子到位.

blocks.en:
In Code, players learned to adjust grip depth and wrist posture to carry cans over the fixed rail and repeat successful interior placements.
In Policy, players learned to lower cans well inside the stationary receiver and coordinate release, settling, and claw withdrawal.
In both baselines, these strategies generally produced repeatable completions, allowing further gains from shorter transfers and pauses.
PlayCraft players also learned to place cans farther inside the deck and leave clearance for withdrawal, but missed grips, rim falls, and interference from rotating cans continued after earlier fast completions.
Persistent correction and recovery delays reduced completion bonuses even after players had learned successful placements.
This inconsistency may explain why PlayCraft trailed at least one baseline on both learning metrics at every intelligence setting.
blocks.zh:
在"代码"中,玩家学会了调整握手深度和手腕姿势,将罐头扛过固定的铁路,并重复成功的室内布置.
在"政策"中,玩家学会了在固定接收器内部把罐子降低,协调释放,安顿,以及爪子退出.
在这两个基线中,这些战略通常会产生可重复的完成,从而能够从较短的转让和暂停中获得进一步的收益。
PlayCraft玩家还学会了在甲板内放置更远的罐头,并离开许可以退出,但错过了握手,轮回坠落,在早期快速完成后旋转罐头的干扰仍在继续.
即使玩家学习了成功的安置,持续的矫正和恢复拖延也减少了完成奖金。
这种不一致可能解释为什么PlayCraft在每个智能环境的学习指标上都至少有一个基线。

blocks.en:
PlayCraft also yielded lower learning gain and slope than the initial game, as shown in Figure 3 .
During the play run preceding the first revision, the agent quickly learned a conservative transfer routine and repeated it reliably.
The first revision added wrist sway and varied the starting positions of the cans, requiring adjustments to braking and pickup approaches.
These additional demands may have made learned routines harder to repeat reliably, which may explain the sharp decline in learning gain and slope after the first revision.
Later revisions partially recovered both measures, but they remained below their initial values in that comparison.
blocks.zh:
PlayCraft的学习收益和斜率也低于最初的游戏,如图3所示.
在第一次改版前的剧情运行中,代理迅速学会了保守的转会常规,并可靠地重复.
第一次修订增加了手腕摇摆,并改变了罐头的起始位置,需要调整制动和取车方式。
这些额外的要求可能使学到的例行公事更难可靠地重复,这可能说明第一次修订后学习增益和斜率急剧下降的原因.
后来的修订部分收回了这两项措施,但在此比较中仍低于其初始值。

blocks.en:
The initial game requires players to collect and deliver packages in order, choose flight paths that conserve battery power, and slow down as they approach each pad.
The PlayCraft player agent quickly settled on a clean route.
In the first round, PlayCraft introduced wind at higher altitudes. The player found a repeatable route through the calm air along the streets.
In the second round, PlayCraft limited shelter to areas behind individual buildings.
The player reported that prolonged coasting could stall progress. The crafter traced this to a speed limit in the code that could abruptly slow the drone on entering a headwind.
The player also completed two deliveries with less damage than in the preceding attempt, but earned the same score.
In the third round, PlayCraft let the drone carry its momentum into a headwind, with drag slowing it gradually.
The revision also awards bonuses for remaining battery power and low damage at each delivery.
Players can build speed in shelter and coast across an exposed stretch.
They can also earn credit for keeping the drone in better condition even if they complete only part of the route.
blocks.zh:
最初的游戏要求玩家按顺序收集和交付包裹,选择节省电池功率的飞行路径,并在接近每个垫时减速.
PlayCraft玩家代理迅速在一条干净的路线上安顿下来.
在第一轮中,PlayCraft引入了较高高度的风. 玩家在沿街的平静空气中发现了一条可重复的路线.
在第二轮中,PlayCraft将避难所限制在个别建筑物后面的地区.
玩家报告说,长时间的海岸化可能会阻碍进展. 制片人追踪到 代码中的速度限制 可能让无人机进入前风时突然减速
玩家还完成了两次送货,损失比之前的尝试少,但得到的分数相同.
在第三轮中,PlayCraft让无人机携带动力进入头风,拖曳速度逐渐放缓.
修订案还奖励每批交付剩余的电池功率和低损坏。
玩家可以在避难所和海岸跨越暴露的拉伸处建立速度.
他们也可以因为让无人机保持更好的状态而获得信用,即使他们只完成了部分航线.

blocks.en:
Code used source analysis and route probes to develop a different trade-off.
Carrying two packages can reduce the number of trips, and delivering while moving can reduce the number of stops.
The extra load makes the drone slower to respond.
Policy controllers spent time waiting for favorable wind or attempting to travel slowly along the ground.
They reached the time cutoff with substantial battery power remaining.
The final revision added runners to the suspended load so the player can tow it more quickly between flights by keeping it aligned on packed snow.
blocks.zh:
代码使用源分析和路由探测器来开发不同的权衡.
搭载两个包裹可以减少出行次数,在移动的同时交付可以减少停站次数.
额外负载使得无人机反应较慢.
政策控制人员花时间等待有利的风,或试图缓慢沿地面行进。
他们到达了限时点,仍然有大量电池。
最终的修订在悬浮负载中增加了跑者,这样玩家就可以通过保持在已打满的雪上对齐,在飞行之间更快地拖动.

blocks.en:
In Code, players adopted batching early and usually used hovering deliveries, learning to coast with heavier loads through open corridors and brake early near obstacles and pads. Once a safe route became reliable, further practice mainly refined pad alignment and produced only small gains.
In Policy, players learned to align the runners, settle the load before turning, and balance cargo preservation against battery use, often abandoning airborne transport after severe cargo damage.
Protecting the more valuable later loads remained difficult, but better handling increased scores even after players could complete the route.
PlayCraft encouraged players to build speed in shelter, coast across exposed gaps, and brake accurately while conserving enough battery for all three deliveries.
At Medium and High, practice produced more reliable routes that reached later deliveries and earned their larger bonuses, which may explain why PlayCraft led on learning gain and slope.
At Low, players described similar energy-saving strategies but usually failed to reach the second delivery because of battery exhaustion or collisions.
This persistent difficulty in execution may explain why PlayCraft trailed the initial game and both baselines on both learning metrics.
blocks.zh:
在"代码"中,玩家采用分批早放,通常使用徘徊送货,通过开放的走廊学习更重的负载,早期在障碍物和垫子附近刹车. 一旦安全路线变得可靠,进一步的做法主要是精细调整垫板,只产生小收益。
在"政策"中,玩家学会了将跑者对齐,在转弯前解决负载,在货物保存与电池使用之间保持平衡,经常在货物严重损坏后放弃空载运输.
保护更值钱的后期负载仍然很困难,但即使在玩家能够完成路由后更好地处理增加的分数.
PlayCraft鼓励玩家在掩蔽处、跨越暴露缺口的海岸以及刹车时精确建造速度,同时为所有三个交货都保留足够的电池。
在中高分,实践产生了更可靠的路线,可以到达后来的交付,并获得更大的奖金,这或许可以解释为什么PlayCraft领导学习增益和坡度.
在Low,玩家描述了类似的节能策略,但通常由于电池耗尽或碰撞而未能达到第二次交付.
这种持续的执行困难可能解释了为什么PlayCraft在两个学习指标上都跟随初始游戏和两个基线.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We presented PlayCraft, an automated framework for making games more engaging by supporting mastery.
A player agent interacts through the same interface as human players, observing the game screen and using the controls to pursue game objectives.
It plays multiple episodes, reviewing its play after each one and carrying its memory from one episode to the next.
PlayCraft uses this play experience to identify gaps between expected and target performance at different proficiency levels and guide changes that enable player performance gain through better decisions and execution.
At each player intelligence setting, fresh evaluation runs showed larger learning gains and steeper learning slopes in most games revised by PlayCraft than in their initial counterparts.
PlayCraft also outperformed the baselines on the macro-average of each metric at every setting.
blocks.zh:
我们提出了PlayCraft, 一种通过支持掌握来让游戏更加参与的自动化框架。
一个玩家代理通过与人类玩家相同的界面进行互动,观察游戏屏幕并利用控制来追求游戏目标.
它播放多集,每集后回顾其剧情,并将记忆从一集传到下一集.
PlayCraft利用这个游戏体验来识别不同熟练程度的预期表现和目标表现之间的差距,并指导通过更好的决策和执行来让玩家获得表现收益的改变.
在每个玩家智能设定中,新鲜评价显示,在PlayCraft修改的大多数游戏中,学习增益更大,学习坡度也比最初的同行要陡.
PlayCraft 也超过了每个设置每个度量的宏观平均值的基线。

blocks.en:
Limitations. PlayCraft assumes that the play and learning patterns of agents resemble those of human players.
Training on human-generated data may help foundation models approximate human decisions, but this assumption remains unverified.
Future work should align agent play with human behavior and test that alignment by comparing the decisions, difficulties, and learning patterns of agents and human players.
Confirming the alignment would make agent play evidence more reliable for game crafting and evaluation.
The second limitation is the cost of playing games that require longer runs.
Increasing the active play budget can require more gameplay time and model inference.
More efficient observation and action planning could make longer runs practical and extend evaluation to a broader range of games.
blocks.zh:
限制。 PlayCraft认为代理商的游戏和学习模式类似于人类玩家的游戏和学习模式.
关于人产生的数据的培训可能有助于基础模型接近人的决定,但这一假设仍未得到证实。
未来的工作应当使代理游戏与人类行为相一致,并通过比较代理和人类角色的决定、困难和学习模式来检验这种协调。
确认调整将使代理商在游戏制作和评价方面玩弄证据更加可靠。
第二个限制是游戏需要更长运行时间的成本.
增加活跃的游戏预算可能需要更多的游戏游戏时间和模型推论.
更有效的观察和行动规划可以使评价更切合实际,并扩大到更广泛的游戏。
